clue_en: Which traveller first described fork use in English in his 1611 account of Italy?
explanation_en: Thomas Coryat described the Italian table fork in his published travels of 1611.

clue_en: Roman tradition assigned the founding of Rome to this year in the eighth century BCE.
explanation_en: The conventional date is 21 April 753 BCE.

clue_en: Legend names this twin as Rome’s founder and first king.
explanation_en: Romulus was said to have killed his brother Remus during the city’s foundation.

clue_en: Name the brother who shared Romulus’s miraculous rescue and upbringing.
explanation_en: The twins were legendary descendants of the Trojan prince Aeneas.

clue_en: In the foundation myth, what animal nursed the abandoned twins?
explanation_en: The she-wolf became one of the enduring symbols of Rome.

clue_en: Romulus was said to have established his settlement on this central Roman hill.
explanation_en: The Palatine later became a favoured site for imperial residences.

clue_en: Despite its familiar name, this Anglo-French conflict lasted about 116 years.
explanation_en: The conventional dates are 1337 to 1453.

clue_en: English kings pursued a claim to the crown of this kingdom.
explanation_en: Dynastic claims and control of French territories drove the conflict.

clue_en: Which young French commander helped lift the English siege of Orléans in 1429?
explanation_en: Her campaign revived the Valois cause and enabled Charles VII’s coronation.

clue_en: The first major English victory of the war came at this battle in 1346.
explanation_en: Edward III’s army defeated a much larger French force.

clue_en: The French victory at this 1453 battle effectively ended the war.
explanation_en: Castillon ended England’s remaining major military position in Gascony.

clue_en: In what year did the Great Fire sweep through central London?
explanation_en: The fire burned from 2 to 6 September 1666.

clue_en: The Great Fire of London began in a bakery on this aptly memorable lane.
explanation_en: Thomas Farriner’s bakery stood on Pudding Lane.

clue_en: The medieval version of this cathedral was destroyed and later rebuilt by Christopher Wren.
explanation_en: Wren’s domed cathedral replaced Old St Paul’s.

clue_en: Which naval administrator recorded the fire in his famous diary?
explanation_en: Pepys observed the disaster and reported it to Charles II.

clue_en: Wren and Robert Hooke designed this tall commemorative column near the fire’s starting point.
response_en: the Monument to the Great Fire of London
explanation_en: The Monument stands close to London Bridge.

clue_en: The coordinated sarin attack on the Tokyo subway occurred in this year.
explanation_en: Attackers released the nerve agent during the morning rush on 20 March.

clue_en: The attack targeted trains converging on the centre of this Japanese capital.
explanation_en: Five coordinated releases struck three subway lines.

clue_en: The perpetrators punctured bags containing this nerve agent on subway trains.
explanation_en: Sarin is an organophosphorus chemical warfare agent.

clue_en: Members of this apocalyptic movement carried out the attack.
explanation_en: Shoko Asahara founded and led Aum Shinrikyo.

clue_en: Aum Shinrikyo’s founder was known by this name.
explanation_en: Asahara was convicted for directing the attack.

clue_en: Abraham Lincoln belonged to this party when elected president in 1860.
explanation_en: Lincoln was the first Republican elected to the presidency.

clue_en: Lincoln built his political career in this state, although he was born in Kentucky.
explanation_en: He served in the Illinois legislature and represented the state in Congress.

clue_en: His 1863 wartime order freeing enslaved people in rebelling areas bears this name.
explanation_en: The order changed the legal status of enslaved people in Confederate-held territory.

clue_en: Which actor assassinated Lincoln at Ford’s Theatre?
explanation_en: Booth shot Lincoln on 14 April 1865.

clue_en: Lincoln’s 1858 Senate debates were against this Democratic rival.
explanation_en: Douglas won the Senate contest, but the debates raised Lincoln’s national profile.

clue_en: Which year is remembered for abnormally cold, wet weather across much of the Northern Hemisphere?
explanation_en: Crop failures and food shortages made it the Year Without a Summer.

clue_en: The climatic disruption followed the enormous eruption of this Indonesian volcano.
explanation_en: Tambora erupted in April 1815 and injected aerosols into the atmosphere.

clue_en: Tambora lies on Sumbawa in this modern country.
explanation_en: The eruption occurred in the Dutch East Indies.

clue_en: A rainy Swiss summer kept Mary Shelley indoors, helping inspire this novel.
explanation_en: Shelley began the story during the gathering at Villa Diodati.

clue_en: Which one-word apocalyptic poem did Lord Byron write under the influence of the abnormal summer of 1816?
explanation_en: The bleak conditions of the Year Without a Summer inspired Byron’s poem Darkness.

clue_en: What spy network supplied George Washington with intelligence from British-held New York?
explanation_en: The ring operated during the American Revolutionary War.

clue_en: Messages sometimes used this chemically hidden medium developed for Washington’s spies.
explanation_en: The ring called it sympathetic stain.

clue_en: Which cavalry officer organised the ring under Washington’s direction?
explanation_en: Tallmadge managed agents and coded correspondence.

clue_en: Abraham Woodhull used this code name within the ring.
explanation_en: Woodhull gathered intelligence on Long Island and in New York.

clue_en: Which numerical code identified a possibly female Culper correspondent whose identity and exact role remain uncertain?
explanation_en: Some sources identify Agent 355 with Anna Strong, while others treat the code as a misunderstood reference in an Abraham Woodhull letter.

clue_en: In which year did Kentucky enter the United States?
explanation_en: Kentucky joined the Union on 1 June 1792.

clue_en: Kentucky entered the Union as which numbered state?
explanation_en: Previously part of Virginia, Kentucky entered the Union on 1 June 1792 as the fifteenth state.

clue_en: Kentucky was separated from this state before admission.
explanation_en: Kentucky had been Virginia’s District of Kentucky before entering the Union as a separate state in 1792.

clue_en: Kentucky is commonly called the state of this blue-tinted pasture grass.
explanation_en: Its “Bluegrass State” nickname refers to Kentucky bluegrass.

clue_en: Name Kentucky’s state capital.
explanation_en: Frankfort became the state capital in 1792.

clue_en: During the attack in 1814, which Washington residence used by President James Madison did British troops burn?
explanation_en: British forces burned the President’s House during their occupation of Washington.

clue_en: The burning of Washington occurred during this conflict between Britain and the United States.
explanation_en: The attack formed part of the War of 1812.

clue_en: British troops also burned the building used by this legislative body.
explanation_en: The Capitol was among the public buildings set on fire.

clue_en: Which first lady helped ensure that important objects were removed from the White House before British troops arrived in 1814?
explanation_en: Dolley Madison helped ensure that important objects were removed before the British entered Washington.

clue_en: The road to Washington opened after the British victory at this Maryland battle.
explanation_en: American forces were defeated at Bladensburg on 24 August 1814.

clue_en: Between 1908 and 1913, Hitler worked as a professional artist in which city?
explanation_en: He lived in Vienna and produced hundreds of works there between 1908 and 1913.

clue_en: Which Vienna institution rejected Hitler’s applications in 1907 and 1908?
response_en: the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna
accepted_variants_en: Vienna Academy of Fine Arts;Academy of Fine Arts
explanation_en: He failed the academy’s entrance examination twice.

clue_en: Hitler’s surviving works concentrate on buildings and streetscapes rather than portraits. What artistic subject did he prefer?
explanation_en: His surviving watercolours and drawings concentrate chiefly on buildings and urban scenes.

clue_en: Most surviving works attributed to Hitler use this water-based painting medium.
explanation_en: He produced many watercolours of buildings and streets.

clue_en: On what date was Adolf Hitler born?
explanation_en: Hitler was born in Braunau am Inn on 20 April 1889.

clue_en: The Neo-Assyrian Empire expanded from a heartland in the north of this ancient region.
explanation_en: Its principal cities lay along and near the Tigris in northern Mesopotamia.

clue_en: Sennacherib made this city, later famed for its library, the imperial capital.
explanation_en: Nineveh remained a royal centre until its destruction in 612 BCE.

clue_en: The great royal library at Nineveh is associated with this seventh-century BCE king.
explanation_en: Thousands of cuneiform tablets from his collection survive.

clue_en: A coalition including Babylonians and this Iranian people captured Nineveh.
explanation_en: The fall of Nineveh in 612 BCE was decisive in the empire’s collapse.

clue_en: Which Shamshi-Adad ruled Assyria around 1563 to 1548 BCE, long before the Neo-Assyrian Empire?
explanation_en: Shamshi-Adad III’s reign is dated to approximately 1563–1548 BCE, centuries before the Neo-Assyrian Empire.

clue_en: The ontological argument for God’s existence is first associated with this medieval thinker.
explanation_en: Anselm set out the argument in the Proslogion.

clue_en: Anselm served from 1093 as archbishop of this English see.
explanation_en: As archbishop, he disputed with English kings over church authority.

clue_en: As of 2026, Anselm’s birthplace of Aosta lies in this country.
explanation_en: Aosta lies in the Italian Alps near the French and Swiss borders.

clue_en: Before becoming archbishop, Anselm was abbot of Bec within this monastic order.
explanation_en: The Abbey of Bec was a major Benedictine centre of learning.

clue_en: Anselm’s title Proslogion is commonly translated by this English word.
explanation_en: The Proslogion contains Anselm’s argument for God’s existence later known as the ontological argument.

clue_en: Which Russian tsar transformed his state during the long war with Sweden?
explanation_en: Peter I founded Saint Petersburg and built a Baltic fleet.

clue_en: The Great Northern War pitted a coalition led by Russia against this Baltic empire.
explanation_en: Sweden entered the conflict as the dominant northern European power.

clue_en: The young warrior king who led Sweden through most of the conflict was this Charles.
explanation_en: Charles XII won early victories but died during a Norwegian campaign.

clue_en: The Great Northern War ended with peace treaties in this year.
explanation_en: The Treaty of Nystad ended the principal war between Russia and Sweden.

clue_en: Russia’s decisive 1709 victory came at this battle in present-day Ukraine.
explanation_en: The Swedish defeat at Poltava reversed the course of the war.

clue_en: The protest wave later called the Arab Spring began in this North African country.
explanation_en: Tunisia’s revolution inspired uprisings across the Arab world.

clue_en: What name was given to the wave of anti-government uprisings across North Africa and the Middle East beginning in late 2010?
explanation_en: The label “Arab Spring” came into wide use in 2011.

clue_en: Egyptian demonstrations centred on this Cairo square.
explanation_en: Tahrir became an international symbol of the 2011 uprising.

clue_en: Which Tunisian leader was forced from power by mass protests in January 2011?
explanation_en: Ben Ali fled Tunisia after twenty-three years in office.

clue_en: The self-immolation of this street vendor became the immediate catalyst for Tunisian protests.
explanation_en: Bouazizi set himself on fire in Sidi Bouzid in December 2010.

clue_en: Who became Haiti’s first ruler after independence?
explanation_en: Dessalines proclaimed Haitian independence in 1804.

clue_en: Haitian independence was proclaimed on the first day of this year.
explanation_en: Dessalines declared independence at Gonaïves on 1 January 1804.

clue_en: Dessalines had served under this revolutionary leader before the French captured him.
explanation_en: Toussaint led the revolution before being deported to France.

clue_en: Before independence, Haiti was the French colony called this.
explanation_en: Saint-Domingue was France’s richest Caribbean plantation colony.

clue_en: Under which regnal name did Jean-Jacques Dessalines rule as Haiti’s first emperor?
explanation_en: Dessalines was proclaimed emperor under the name Jacques I in 1804.

clue_en: How many crewed missions have landed people on the Moon?
explanation_en: Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17 achieved crewed lunar landings.

clue_en: Which mission made the first crewed lunar landing?
explanation_en: Apollo 11 landed in July 1969.

clue_en: All six crewed lunar landings belonged to this United States space programme.
explanation_en: NASA’s Apollo programme carried out the landings.

clue_en: Which Apollo mission made the most recent crewed Moon landing, in 1972?
explanation_en: Apollo 17 was the sixth and most recent crewed lunar landing.

clue_en: Apollo 11 landed in the lunar plain whose Latin name is Mare Tranquillitatis. Give its English name.
explanation_en: The lunar module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquillity.

clue_en: Japan’s surrender meant that this planned Allied invasion of the home islands was never carried out.
explanation_en: Downfall comprised Operation Olympic against Kyushu and Operation Coronet against Honshu.

clue_en: Operation Coronet targeted the Tokyo Plain on which Japanese island?
explanation_en: Coronet was the planned invasion of Honshu near Tokyo.

clue_en: Operation Olympic would have targeted this southernmost main Japanese island.
explanation_en: Airfields on Kyushu were intended to support the later attack.

clue_en: The first phase, aimed at southern Kyushu, had this Olympic name.
explanation_en: Olympic was scheduled for November 1945.

clue_en: The planned assault on the Tokyo plain was named for this coronet.
explanation_en: Coronet was planned for spring 1946.

clue_en: Which two countries confronted each other in the so-called Lobster War?
explanation_en: Brazil and France disputed lobster fishing rights off Brazil.

clue_en: The dispute centred on fishing for this crustacean.
explanation_en: French boats sought spiny lobsters on Brazil’s continental shelf.

clue_en: The naval confrontation took place in this ocean off northeastern Brazil.
explanation_en: The grounds lay off northeastern Brazil, where French fishing boats challenged Brazil’s continental-shelf claim.

clue_en: The Lobster War ran from 1961 to this year.
explanation_en: The active naval confrontation ended in 1963, while the bilateral settlement agreement followed in December 1964.

clue_en: On what date did Brazil and France sign the agreement that settled the Lobster War?
explanation_en: The bilateral agreement ended the fishing-rights dispute after several years of naval confrontation off northeastern Brazil.

clue_en: Which County Mayo village became a pilgrimage centre after a reported apparition in 1879?
explanation_en: Witnesses reported an apparition beside the parish church at Knock.

clue_en: In which year was the Knock apparition reported?
explanation_en: The event was reported on 21 August 1879.

clue_en: Knock lies in which western Irish county?
explanation_en: Knock is both a Roman Catholic pilgrimage site and a national shrine in County Mayo.

clue_en: Knock developed into a major destination for travellers making this religious journey.
explanation_en: Pilgrims visit the County Mayo shrine associated with the reported apparition of 1879.

clue_en: Witnesses said they saw the Virgin Mary, Saint Joseph, and this evangelist.
explanation_en: Some witnesses said Saint John appeared to preach while holding an open book; others did not report the book.

clue_en: The original restaurant opened in this Kansas city.
explanation_en: Its small building later moved to Wichita State University.

clue_en: The first Pizza Hut restaurant opened in this year.
explanation_en: The Carney brothers opened it while studying at university.

clue_en: These two brothers founded the chain.
explanation_en: They borrowed money from their mother to start the restaurant.

clue_en: The first franchised location opened in 1959 in this Kansas capital.
explanation_en: Expansion began only a year after the original shop opened.

clue_en: Pizza Hut’s original Italian-chef mascot had which alliterative name?
explanation_en: Pizza Pete was the company’s original chef mascot before the red-roof emblem replaced him.

clue_en: What collective name is given to the ancient trade networks linking East Asia with Central Asia and the Mediterranean world?
explanation_en: The term covers interconnected overland and maritime routes.

clue_en: The luxury textile that supplied the network’s modern name originated in this country.
explanation_en: Chinese silk travelled westward through many intermediaries.

clue_en: Monks and merchants helped carry this Indian religion eastward along the routes into China.
explanation_en: Trade corridors also transmitted religions, art, and technologies.

clue_en: Which city in modern Uzbekistan became a celebrated crossroads on the overland routes?
explanation_en: Under Timur, Samarkand became one of the Islamic world’s most important trade centres and cultural entrepôts.

clue_en: The expression “Silk Road” was popularised in the nineteenth century by geographer Ferdinand von this surname.
explanation_en: Ferdinand von Richthofen used the German term Seidenstraße.

clue_en: The Fourth Crusade began in 1202 and ended with the sack of Constantinople in this year.
explanation_en: Crusaders captured and sacked Constantinople in April 1204.

clue_en: Instead of reaching the Holy Land, crusaders captured this Christian imperial capital.
explanation_en: The city was taken and plundered in April 1204.

clue_en: Ships and financing came chiefly from this maritime republic.
explanation_en: The crusaders’ unpaid debt to Venice redirected the expedition.

clue_en: Which pope called the Fourth Crusade in 1198?
explanation_en: Innocent intended an expedition to recover Jerusalem through Egypt.

clue_en: After the conquest, the crusaders established this polity in Constantinople.
explanation_en: The Latin Empire lasted until Byzantine forces retook the city in 1261.

clue_en: The United States commemorates the adoption of its Declaration of Independence on this date.
explanation_en: The Second Continental Congress adopted the declaration in Philadelphia.
source_title: United States Declaration of Independence — Wikipedia

clue_en: Which Virginia delegate drafted the declaration’s best-known text?
explanation_en: Jefferson wrote the initial draft for the Committee of Five.
source_title: United States Declaration of Independence — Wikipedia

clue_en: The grievances in the declaration were directed against this British monarch.
explanation_en: The text accused George III of establishing tyranny over the colonies.
source_title: United States Declaration of Independence — Wikipedia

clue_en: Which assembly adopted the Declaration of Independence?
explanation_en: Delegates from the colonies met at the Pennsylvania State House.
source_title: United States Declaration of Independence — Wikipedia

clue_en: Which Philadelphia printer produced the declaration’s first broadside copies?
explanation_en: The Dunlap broadsides spread the adopted text quickly.
source_title: United States Declaration of Independence — Wikipedia

clue_en: The Boxing Day earthquake and Indian Ocean tsunami occurred in this year.
explanation_en: The disaster struck on 26 December 2004.
source_title: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami — Wikipedia

clue_en: The undersea rupture began off the west coast of this Indonesian island.
explanation_en: The epicentre was near northern Sumatra.
source_title: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami — Wikipedia

clue_en: The disaster accelerated creation of a regional system to warn coastal communities about these waves.
explanation_en: An Indian Ocean tsunami warning system became operational after 2004.
source_title: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami — Wikipedia

clue_en: As assessed in 2026, the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake ranked among the strongest recorded on this magnitude scale.
explanation_en: Estimates place the earthquake around magnitude 9.1 to 9.3.
source_title: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami — Wikipedia

clue_en: The earthquake occurred where the Indian Plate is forced beneath this smaller plate.
explanation_en: Movement along the Sunda megathrust displaced the seafloor.
source_title: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami — Wikipedia

category_name_en: Sandra Day O'Connor on the Court
clue_en: True or false: Ronald Reagan was the first US president to appoint a woman to the Supreme Court.
explanation_en: Reagan appointed Sandra Day O’Connor in 1981, making him the first president to appoint a woman to the Court.

category_name_en: Sandra Day O'Connor on the Court
clue_en: O’Connor joined the Supreme Court in this year.
explanation_en: She took her judicial oath in September 1981.

category_name_en: Sandra Day O'Connor on the Court
clue_en: Before her federal appointment, O’Connor was a judge and legislator in this state.
explanation_en: She became the first woman to serve as majority leader of an American state senate.

category_name_en: Sandra Day O'Connor on the Court
clue_en: Which justice succeeded O’Connor after her retirement in 2006?
explanation_en: Alito was confirmed to O’Connor’s seat in January 2006.

category_name_en: Sandra Day O'Connor on the Court
clue_en: O’Connor filled the seat vacated by this justice.
explanation_en: Stewart retired from the Supreme Court in 1981.

clue_en: Which country has been invaded by powers including Alexander’s Macedonians, the Mongols, Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States?
explanation_en: Alexander’s Macedonian Empire, the Mongol Empire, the British Empire, the Soviet Union, and the United States all invaded Afghanistan.

clue_en: The Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan in December of this year.
explanation_en: The Soviet Union had supported the Afghan government after the 1978 Saur Revolution; its 40th Army entered on 24 December 1979.

clue_en: Britain fought three nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century conflicts collectively known by this name.
explanation_en: The Anglo-Afghan Wars pitted British India against Afghanistan.

clue_en: Invaders travelling from Afghanistan toward India often used which mountain pass?
explanation_en: The Khyber Pass provided a route from Afghanistan into the Indian subcontinent.

clue_en: Alexander the Great’s conquests included the Afghan region known by which ancient name?
explanation_en: Alexander settled the conquered region with Ionian veterans; after his death, Bactria came under Seleucus’s rule.

clue_en: Allied forces landed in Normandy on this date in 1944.
explanation_en: The date is commonly called D-Day.

clue_en: Which American landing beach saw especially severe casualties on D-Day?
explanation_en: Omaha Beach lay between Utah and the British beaches.

clue_en: What has historical research found about claims that Operation Fortitude used inflatable dummy tanks?
accepted_variants_en: no evidence;there is no evidence they were used;no evidence of their use
explanation_en: Fortitude relied largely on double agents and false radio traffic; no evidence has been found that it used inflatable tanks.

clue_en: Canadian forces landed at this beach.
explanation_en: Juno lay between Gold and Sword.

clue_en: Sword Beach stretched eastward to which port town at the mouth of the River Orne?
explanation_en: Sword Beach extended along the coast to Ouistreham at its eastern end.

clue_en: By what three-letter abbreviation is the National Security Agency known?
explanation_en: The agency adopted the initials NSA when it was established in 1952 as the successor to the Armed Forces Security Agency.

clue_en: The NSA operates within which cabinet department of the United States government?
accepted_variants_en: Department of Defense;US Department of Defense;DoD
explanation_en: The National Security Agency is an intelligence agency within the Department of Defense.

clue_en: The NSA’s core intelligence specialty is intercepting and analysing communications, known by this compound term.
explanation_en: Signals intelligence is commonly abbreviated SIGINT.

clue_en: On what date was the United States National Security Agency formally established?
explanation_en: A presidential directive established the NSA on 4 November 1952.

clue_en: Which three-word organisation created in 1949 directly preceded the NSA?
explanation_en: The NSA replaced the Armed Forces Security Agency in 1952.

clue_en: True or false: Voltaire wrote “I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it.”
explanation_en: The sentence was written by Evelyn Beatrice Hall as a summary of Voltaire’s attitude.

clue_en: Which English writer actually composed the sentence commonly misattributed to Voltaire?
explanation_en: Evelyn Beatrice Hall wrote the sentence in her biography of Voltaire’s circle.

clue_en: In which 1906 book did the sentence first appear?
explanation_en: Hall published the sentence in The Friends of Voltaire under her pen name, S. G. Tallentyre.

clue_en: Hall published the book under which pseudonym?
explanation_en: Evelyn Beatrice Hall used the pen name S. G. Tallentyre.

clue_en: The sentence appears in a chapter about which French philosopher whose book On the Mind was burned?
explanation_en: Hall used the sentence while describing Voltaire’s attitude toward Helvétius.

clue_en: Which surviving royal palace near Richmond was closely associated with Henry VIII?
explanation_en: The palace stands on the Thames southwest of central London.

clue_en: The palace gardens contain a famous example of this hedge-lined puzzle.
explanation_en: The Hampton Court Maze was planted around the turn of the eighteenth century.

clue_en: Henry VIII belonged to this royal dynasty.
explanation_en: Tudor additions remain central to Hampton Court’s appearance.

clue_en: Which cardinal began transforming Hampton Court into a great palace?
explanation_en: Wolsey presented the palace to Henry VIII as his political position weakened.

clue_en: Which architect designed major Baroque rebuilding for William III and Mary II?
explanation_en: Wren’s south and east fronts contrast with the Tudor courts.
